# War Powers and Foreign Policy

## By the end of today

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
You will be able to explain the 1789 break on war power, how later practice shifted toward the executive, and why Congress rarely takes the power back.
:::

## Where this fits

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Concentrated force is most concentrated in war.
:::

That is why the Founders tried to split the decision from the command.

## The 1789 break

![1789 war power: Britain versus the United States](../../assets/1789_war.jfif){fig-alt="Contrast of British royal war prerogative in 1789 with U.S. congressional power to declare war" width="90%"}

## Article I

Congress:

- Declares war
- Raises and supports armies
- No army appropriation longer than two years
- Maintains a navy
- Issues letters of marque and reprisal

## Article II

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.7em;"}
The President is Commander in Chief.
:::

## The intended split

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Congress decides whether the nation is at war. The President conducts the war Congress has authorized.
:::

## The purse again

![Power of the purse](../../assets/the_purse.jfif){fig-alt="Purse constraint on executive military action" width="75%"}

No money, no war machine.

## What changed

Declarations became rare.

Authorizations, resolutions, and “hostilities” short of declared war became the working law.

## War Powers Resolution, 1973

Attempt at “collective judgment” after Vietnam.

48-hour report. 60-day clock. Consultation.

## The standing fight

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
What counts as “hostilities”? Who gets to decide that word?
:::

## Pattern, not party

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Both parties expand the office when they hold it.
:::

Congress complains, funds the operation, and rarely forces a clean stop.

## Case pattern: capture operations

Panama, 1989: Noriega.

Venezuela, January 2026: Maduro.

Law-enforcement goal + military means.

## Case pattern: the clock

Iran, February 2026– : strikes, reports, ceasefire claims, concurrent resolutions.

The 60-day clock is a political deadline more than an off-switch.

## Courts

War-powers disputes are often treated as political questions.

The fight stays in Congress and in elections.

## Recap

- 1789: declare war is a legislative power
- Command is executive
- Modern practice stretched “hostilities”
- Tools exist; political will is the scarce resource

## Top Hat

- T/F: In 1789, the power to declare war was given to Congress, not the President.
- MC: The War Powers Resolution’s 60-day clock is best described as:
- Likert: “Capture operations against a foreign head of state should count as hostilities under the War Powers Resolution.”
